raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation Currently, `AscendAttnBackend` inherits `needs_cpu_seq_lens=True`. However, for DSA models that don't actually require `seq_lens_cpu`, we can bypass this dependency to reduce—or even eliminate—the CPU-bound bubbles. This PR sets `needs_cpu_seq_lens=False` for `AscendAttnBackend` when running DSA models. ## Modifications - Added a `needs_cpu_seq_lens` member variable to both `AscendAttnBackend` and `AscendAttnMultiStepDraftBackend`. It is set to False when running DSA models without the HybridSWA feature, which enables the optimization introduced by this PR. - Added branches for `needs_cpu_seq_lens is False` at device synchronization points within `AscendAttnBackend`, allowing device-side tensors to be used directly in computations. - Moved the `all_reduce` communication in `EAGLEDraftNpuGraphRunner.can_run_graph` to the CPU to eliminate blocking waits. ~~This PR builds upon PR #36472 and should be merged after it.~~ The predecessor to this PR is #21895. Both aim to eliminate the CPU-bound overhead during Draft execution, and both are exclusively applicable to DSA models. Clearly, directly adapting `needs_cpu_seq_lens=False` is the superior approach, as it introduces no additional computation and preserves the original execution flow. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k full(1319) accuracy: 0.951 ``` python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1400 --num-shots 2 --data-path ./gsm8k.jsonl --max-new-tokens 1024 --parallel 32 ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling | Compare |
